sources.citation: McLaughlin, Carey Elizabeth. 2013 [2012 GIAL MA thesis]. A Salience Scheme for Hmong Soud: Types of Foreground and Background Information in Narrative Discourse. SIL e-Books 55. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.tag: read: notes on stress
sources.note: Not about sfm: Hmong Soud is Northern Hua Miao of Honghe (Yunnan); fn.8 explicitly says it is 'a different group from.. the Small Flowery Miao (Gha-mu)'. The word 'stress' does not occur. The earlier scan's attribution of this thesis to Gha-Mu was a misreading of the Glottolog classification comment.

sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: For the 2nd vernacular only location and speaker count (p.104: '第二土语使用人数约有六万。通行在贵州省纳雍、赫章两县和六盘水市的水城特区'); no phonology of this vernacular. sources.citation: Jackson, Eric. 2016. Small Flowery Miao [sfm] for Pollard Script analysis. Unpublished manuscript, SIL International (cited in Cheuk 2017, Unicode L2/17-345, bibliography and acknowledgements: 'Dr. Eric Jackson, Linguistics Consultant in Phonetics and Phonology for SIL International, for recording and analysing the sounds of three language groups').
sources.tag: likely states tone; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: A phonetic/phonological analysis of Small Flowery Miao made to map its sounds onto Pollard-script letters; since the script writes tone by vowel-sign position / tone marks (Cheuk 2017: 'positioning tone marks (U+16F8F.U+16F92) to indicate different tones'), the analysis must enumerate the sfm tone categories. Basis: citation and acknowledgement in Cheuk 2017 only; the ms itself is not online. Obtainable only by request to SIL East Asia Group / the author.

sources.note: CNKI portal record shows the opening of the text instead of an abstract: it characterises vernaculars by reflexes of proto sound classes and refers to tone categories ('..出现在b调或4、6调了不带鼻冠了塞音、塞擦音、塞边音声..'), i.e. phonological (incl. tonal) diagnostics per Guizhou vernacular; likely gives the tone-category behaviour (e.g. breathy/aspirated reflexes in tones 4/6, prenasalisation loss by tone) for the 2nd vernacular. Full text on CNKI only (login).
